Do decision makers decide alike?

Source: R/rvw.R
dmvar.Rd

When cases are shared among several decision makers (reviewers, judges, panels), the share of their decisions that go one way should differ by no more than chance if the cases are alike. dmvar() gives each decision maker's rate with its exact interval and the share of all such decisions that are theirs, the chi-square test that the rates are equal, the same test without the decision makers who decided few cases, and the test with each decision maker left out in turn, which shows whether one of them makes the difference. Sprott, Doob and Iftene (2021, Tables 10 and 11) found the share of reviews that kept a person in a Structured Intervention Unit to run from 37.5% to over 75% across twelve decision makers, with and without the one who had decided fewest.

Usage

dmvar(dec, dm, out, nmin = 5, level = 0.95)

Arguments

dec

The decision in each case: labels.

dm

The decision maker of each case: labels.

out

The decision whose rate is compared: one of the labels of dec.

nmin

The cases below which a decision maker is left out of the second test: a whole number from 1.

level

The level of the exact intervals: one number between 0 and 1.

Value

A list: tab, a data frame with one row per decision maker (dm, n, k the decisions that were out, rate, lo, hi, share of all such decisions); test, two rows (set: "all" and "n >= nmin", with m the decision makers, stat, df, p and low the cells with an expected count under 5); drop, one row per decision maker left out (dm, stat, df, p); out; and level.

Details

The test takes the cases as shared without regard to who decides; where they are not, a difference may be one of the cases and not of the decision makers (jdgiv() and jmono() treat that question).

References

Sprott, J. B., Doob, A. N. and Iftene, A. (2021). Do Independent External Decision Makers Ensure that "An Inmate's Confinement in a Structured Intervention Unit Is to End as Soon as Possible"? Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University, 10 May 2021.

Examples

dm <- rep(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), c(30, 28, 25, 4))
dec <- rep(c("remain", "remove", "remain", "remove", "remain", "remove",
             "remain"), c(24, 6, 10, 18, 15, 10, 4))
dmvar(dec, dm, out = "remain")
#> $tab
#>   dm  n  k      rate        lo        hi     share
#> 1  a 30 24 0.8000000 0.6143335 0.9228645 0.4528302
#> 2  b 28 10 0.3571429 0.1864067 0.5593497 0.1886792
#> 3  c 25 15 0.6000000 0.3866535 0.7887452 0.2830189
#> 4  d  4  4 1.0000000 0.3976354 1.0000000 0.0754717
#> 
#> $test
#>         set m     stat df           p low
#> 1       all 4 14.63426  3 0.002157435   2
#> 2 n >= nmin 3 11.75893  2 0.002796286   0
#> 
#> $drop
#>   dm      stat df            p
#> 1  a  7.270408  2 0.0263785505
#> 2  b  4.356395  2 0.1132454520
#> 3  c 14.672556  2 0.0006514707
#> 4  d 11.758926  2 0.0027962859
#> 
#> $out
#> [1] "remain"
#> 
#> $level
#> [1] 0.95
#>
